title: Inference without Interference: Disaggregate LLM Inference for Mixed Downstream Workloads
technique: TetriInfer: fixed-size chunked prefill, disaggregated prefill/decode instances, two-level scheduling with length-prediction (SJF prefill; decentralized load-balanced decode placement), instance flipping

optimized_metrics.evidence: The prefill instance's scheduler is crucial for improving the prefill phase's latency and throughput
FCFS can lead to head-of-line blocking and high average job completion time (JCT) when requests have long prompts ... By design, they can achieve lower JCT compared to FCFS.

headline_claim.text: it uses 38% less resources all the while lowering average TTFT and average JCT by 97% and 47%, respectively.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 5, Fig 17 decode throughput, interference characterization

metric_definitions.definition_quote: resource usage time represents the aggregated wall time that the prefill and decode instances use to run a particular workload. For example, the resource usage time is 3 seconds if we run prefill in in 1 second and decode in 2 seconds. For vLLM, it is the total runtime since it couples prefill and decode.
metric_definitions.notes: cost proxy = instance-time, summed over prefill and decode instances

metric_definitions.definition_quote: efficiency as in performance per dollar (perf/$)
metric_definitions.notes: never formally defined; appears to combine JCT (performance) with resource usage time (cost): e.g. LPLD 'resource usage time is comparable' and JCT -40% gives perf/$ 1.4x

used without formal definition; 'Comparing TTFT indicates whether TetriInfer's prefill scheduler and chunked prefill are effective.' Evaluation is of a 128-request batch so queueing in the prefill scheduler is included
used without formal definition; 'Comparing JCT indicates whether TetriInfer's disaggregated prefill and decode design and two-level decode scheduling are effective.'

load_regime: offline batch-style: 128 requests per workload type (five mixes: LPLD, LPHD, HPLD, HPHD, Mixed) from ShareGPT; no request-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: disaggregation uses 2x hardware cards; HPHD gains small ('the overhead we introduce cannot be offset'); LPHD improves perf/$ only 1.1x; large-LLM parallel mode may lower throughput by ~10%
hardware: 4x NVIDIA V100-32GB; emulated 200Gbps RoCE / 300GBps NVLink KV transfer ('mock mechanism')
workloads: ShareGPT samples, 128 requests per workload; heavy prefill >512 tokens, heavy decode >128 tokens
extractor_notes: Averages only: no P99/percentile objective and no SLOs. TTFT, JCT used without definition; perf/$ not formally defined. Evaluation is closed-loop 128-request batches, so 'JCT' is per-request completion time within that batch.
load_class_quote: 'In Figure 15, we run 128 requests' per workload mix (five mixes, ShareGPT samples); no request-rate sweep (§5, txt l.~734)
